title: End-design-free rebooting of terminally redundant Pseudomonas phages
author: Yokoyama, Kimura, et al.

The purpose of this section is to prepare a phage stock by rapid purification for the extraction of phage DNA in the following sections.1.Incubate host bacteria overnight in LB broth at 37°C.2.Dilute the phage stock to the desired dilution rate in SM buffer.Note: Diluted phages (approximately 106 PFU/mL) can be used.3.Warm LB agar (3 plates) in an incubator.4.Prepare 3 mL of LB top agar in each tube and keep warm at 50°C.5.Mix 110 μL of host bacteria cultured overnight and 110 μL of phage diluent in a 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube.6.Add 200 μL of mixture (prepared in Step 5) to 3 mL of LB top agar placed at 50°C.7.As a negative control, mix 100 μL of host bacteria with 3 mL of LB top agar.8.Before the prepared LB top agar solidifies, quickly pour it over the LB agar and tilt the plate to distribute it evenly. Let the plate sit undisturbed until the agar solidifies completely.9.Once the agar has solidified, invert the plate and incubate it overnight at 37°C.Note: The solidification time is approximately 5 min, and if the agar is not fully solidified, the LB top agar may shift or detach from the plate surface.10.The next day, check the LB agar plates and pick up those that are lysed in a lacy manner.11.Add 3 mL of SM buffer to each of the three LB agar plates showing lace-like lysis and incubate them at 37°C for at least 30 min.12.Collect the lysate solution from the LB agar medium into a 50-mL centrifuge tube by gently scraping it off the top agar using a disposable bacteria spreader.13.Centrifuge the top agar mixed with the lysate solution at 6,000 × g for 10 min.14.Filter-sterilize the supernatant lysate solution using a 0.45-μm syringe filter unit (Advantec, Tokyo, Japan).15.Carefully pour the supernatant lysate into a centrifugal filter unit (Merck Millipore, Burlington, MA) and add 10 mL of SM buffer.16.Securely close the lid and place the centrifuge tube in the centrifuge with the filter face oriented outward, and centrifuge it at 4,000 × g for 10 min.17.Check the filtration level of the lysate solution and centrifuge until 1 mL remains in the upper chamber. Repeat the centrifugation briefly, ensuring that the lysate solution does not completely drain into the lower layer.18.Repeat the same procedure three times, substituting with SM buffer.Note: Ensure that the lysate in the upper chamber does not completely drain into the lower chamber.Note: Because the filtration speed varies based on the type and titer of the phage, it is important to frequently monitor the progression of filtration by performing short centrifugation intervals.19.When only 1 mL of lysate remains in the upper chamber, discard the lower layer and carefully collect 1 mL of the phage solution in the upper chamber into a 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube simultaneously washing the inner filter section with the remaining phage solution in the upper chamber.20.Store the collected phage solution at 4°C.Note: The collected phage solution will maintain titers for approximately 1 month, depending on the type of phage.Note: Phage samples stored for more than 1 month may have decreased titers; hence, it is recommended to check the titers again.

This section describes the method for extracting the phage genome from the obtained phage stock. In the rebooting of ΦR26, obtaining high-purity, mutation-free DNA at a sufficient yield was crucial for successful genome reconstruction. Although this protocol was optimized for ΦR26, it can also be applied to other phages. Ensuring the integrity and purity of the extracted DNA is a fundamental requirement for phage rebooting, making this step a critical component of the overall process.31.Prepare 900 μL of sample adjusted to 1010 PFU/ml of the phage solution obtained in the previous section. Use SM buffer for phage dilution.32.Digest exogenous DNA such as bacterial genomes in the sample using the TURBO DNA-free kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.33.Add 20 μL of Turbo DNase and 100 μL of DNase buffer to the sample and incubate it at 37°C for at least 30 min.34.Add 4 μL of DNase inactivation buffer and incubate the sample at room temperature with 2–3 times of inverted mixing occasionally for 5 min.35.Centrifuge the sample at 10,000 × g for 2 min and collect the supernatant except for the precipitated DNase inactivation buffer.36.Extract the phage DNA using the phage DNA isolation kit (Norgen, Thorold, ON, Canada) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.37.Determine the DNA concentration of the phage genome sample using Biospec-Nano (Shimadzu, Kyoto, Japan).38.Dilute the phage genome sample with nuclease-free water to 100 ng/μL.39.Store the phage genome sample at −20°C.Pause point: For long-term storage, we recommend storing the sample at −80°C.Note: Repeated freezing and thawing can damage the phage DNA. To minimize this risk, store the samples in small aliquots to reduce the frequency of freezing and thawing.

For gel extraction (if required).54.Mix Novel Juice 6× loading buffer (GeneDireX) with the remaining 40 μL of the DNA fragment sample not soaked in EtBr for gel extraction.55.Mix 1 g of SeaKem ME Agarose (Lonza, Basel, Switzerland) with TAE buffer. Heat the solution to completely dissolve ME agarose in TAE buffer.56.After mixing the Seakem ME Agarose (Lonza), prepare the gels for electrophoresis using a gel maker (Mupid, Tokyo, Japan) so that the thickness is 3–5 mm.57.Pour 1× TAE buffer into the electrophoresis tank so that the top of the gel is soaked approximately 1 mm.58.Apply the DNA fragment sample mixed with Novel Juice to the electrophoresis wells.59.Set the electrophoresis conditions to 100 V for 35 min.60.Cut out the desired bands using a scalpel under a BLooK LED Transilluminator.Note: To prevent DNA damage, we recommend using fluorescence-based imaging during gel extraction.61.Extract DNA from the gel according to the protocol of the QIAquick Gel Extraction Kit (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany).62.Purify all DNA fragment samples according to the protocol of the QIAquick PCR Purification Kit (Qiagen).63.Elute the purified DNA fragments in 100 μL of nuclease-free water.64.Add 3.3 μL of 3 M sodium acetate and 2 μL of etachinmate (Nippon Gene) to each reaction solution.65.Mix the sample by vortexing.66.Add 250 μL of 100% EtOH and mix thoroughly by vortexing.67.Centrifuge the sample at 12,000 × g for 5 min and discard the supernatant.Note: If the desired concentration cannot be achieved from a single gel extraction, perform multiple extractions and concentrate the DNA using ethanol precipitation. To maximize assembly efficiency, ensure that the molar variation between fragments is within ±0.005 pmol.Note: At this time point, do not aspirate the precipitated white pellet DNA by mistake.68.Add 1 mL of 70% EtOH and pipette gently to peel off the DNA precipitate adhering to the wall surface.69.Centrifuge the sample at 12,000 × g for 2 min and discard the supernatant.70.Turn the tube upside down and air-dry for 15 min.71.When sufficiently evaporated, dissolve the DNA in 30 μL of nuclease-free water.72.Measure the DNA concentration using Biospec-Nano (Shimadzu).73.Dilute the DNA with nuclease-free water to a concentration of 0.05 pmol/fragment.Note: The DNA purification step in this section serves to eliminate the template phage DNA used during PCR, thereby preventing unintended rebooting of the original template phage. Our validation confirmed that the sequential purification procedures effectively reduced residual template DNA to undetectable levels.

steps.title: Prepare SM buffer
steps.instruction: Weigh MgSO4·7H2O (2.0 g), NaCl (5.8 g), gelatin (0.1 g) and dissolve in distilled water, add 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 8.0 to 50 mM, bring volume to 1 L, autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min, store at 20‑25 °C for up to 1 year.

steps.title: Prepare LB broth
steps.instruction: Weigh tryptone (10 g), NaCl (10 g), yeast extract (5 g), dissolve in distilled water, bring volume to 1 L, autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min, store at 20‑25 °C for up to 2 months.

steps.title: Prepare 50× TAE buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve Tris base (242 g) for 2 M, acetic acid (57.1 mL) for 1 M, and EDTA disodium salt dihydrate (18.6 g) for 50 mM in distilled water, bring to 1 L, store at 20‑25 °C for up to 1 year.

steps.title: Prepare LB top agar
steps.instruction: Weigh tryptone (10 g), NaCl (10 g), yeast extract (5 g), agarose (5 g), dissolve in distilled water, bring to 1 L, autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min, store at 50 °C for up to 2 months.

steps.title: Prepare LB agar plates
steps.instruction: Weigh tryptone (10 g), NaCl (10 g), yeast extract (5 g), agar (15 g), dissolve in distilled water, bring to 1 L, autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min, pour into flat Petri dishes, let solidify at room temperature, store at 4 °C for up to 2 months; dry plates if water droplets are present before use.

steps.title: Prepare phage stock
steps.instruction: Perform rapid phage purification to obtain high‑titer lysate for DNA extraction.

substeps.instruction: Incubate host bacteria overnight in LB broth at 37 °C.
Dilute phage stock in SM buffer to ~10⁶ PFU mL⁻¹.
Warm three LB agar plates in an incubator.
Warm 3 mL LB top agar per tube at 50 °C.
Mix 110 µL overnight host culture with 110 µL phage dilution in a 1.5‑mL tube.
Add 200 µL of the mixture to 3 mL warm LB top agar.
Negative control: mix 100 µL host with 3 mL LB top agar.
Before solidification, pour top agar over LB agar, tilt to spread evenly; let solidify (~5 min).
Incubate plates inverted overnight at 37 °C.
Next day, select plates showing lace‑like lysis.
Add 3 mL SM buffer to each lytic plate, incubate 37 °C ≥30 min.
Scrape top agar‑lysate into a 50‑mL tube with a disposable spreader.
Centrifuge at 6,000 × g for 10 min.
Filter supernatant through a 0.45‑µm syringe filter.
Transfer filtrate to a centrifugal filter unit, add 10 mL SM buffer.
Centrifuge filter unit at 4,000 × g for 10 min with filter face outward.
Repeat short centrifugation cycles, monitoring progress, until ~1 mL remains in the upper chamber; repeat three times, each time adding SM buffer.
When 1 mL remains, discard lower chamber, collect the 1 mL phage solution into a 1.5‑mL tube, washing the filter with the remaining solution.
Store phage solution at 4 °C (stable ~1 month).

steps.title: Extract phage DNA
steps.instruction: Purify high‑quality phage genomic DNA from the prepared stock.

substeps.instruction: Adjust 900 µL of phage stock to 10¹⁰ PFU mL⁻¹ with SM buffer.
Treat with TURBO DNA‑free kit: add 20 µL Turbo DNase and 100 µL DNase buffer, incubate 37 °C ≥30 min.
Add 4 µL DNase inactivation buffer, incubate at room temperature 5 min with occasional inversion (2–3×).
Centrifuge 10,000 × g for 2 min; collect supernatant.
Extract DNA using Norgen phage DNA isolation kit per manufacturer’s instructions.
Measure DNA concentration with Biospec‑Nano.
Dilute DNA to 100 ng µL⁻¹ with nuclease‑free water.
Store DNA at –20 °C (long‑term –80 °C; aliquot to avoid freeze‑thaw).

steps.title: Amplify DNA fragments by PCR
steps.instruction: Generate ten overlapping ~7 kb (fragments 1‑9) and one ~2.7 kb (fragment 10) PCR products for assembly.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 50 µL PCR master mix per reaction: 25 µL PrimeStar Max (2×), 1‑2 µL template DNA (10 ng µL⁻¹), 3 µL forward primer (2 µM), 3 µL reverse primer (2 µM), add nuclease‑free water to 50 µL.
Run PCR: 98 °C 120 s; 35 cycles of 98 °C 10 s, 65 °C 45 s, 72 °C 120 s; final extension 72 °C 120 s; hold 4 °C.
If needed, optimise annealing temperature by gradient PCR or extend extension time for low yield.

steps.title: Run agarose gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Verify PCR product sizes and purity on a 1 % agarose gel.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1 % agarose (1 g agarose S) in 1× TAE, heat to dissolve.
Pour gel (3‑5 mm thick) into electrophoresis tank, ensure buffer covers gel top by ~1 mm.
Mix 10 µL PCR product with 2 µL 6× loading buffer.
Load 1‑kb DNA ladder and samples into wells.
Run at 100 V for 35 min (keep bath ≤40 °C; replace buffer if overheated).
Stain gel in ethidium bromide for 15 min (cover with foil).
Image under UV; note band positions.

steps.title: Extract DNA from gel (if needed)
steps.instruction: Purify specific PCR fragments when nonspecific bands are observed.

substeps.instruction: Mix remaining 40 µL PCR sample with Novel Juice 6× loading buffer.
Prepare 1 % SeaKem ME agarose in 1× TAE, melt, pour 3‑5 mm gel.
Load samples, run 100 V for 35 min.
Excise desired bands under blue LED transilluminator.
Extract DNA using QIAquick Gel Extraction Kit.
Purify all fragments with QIAquick PCR Purification Kit; elute in 100 µL nuclease‑free water.
Add 3.3 µL 3 M sodium acetate and 2 µL Etachinmate, vortex.
Add 250 µL 100 % ethanol, vortex, centrifuge 12,000 × g 5 min, discard supernatant.
Add 1 mL 70 % ethanol, gently invert to wash pellet, centrifuge 12,000 × g 2 min, discard supernatant.
Air‑dry pellet 15 min, dissolve in 30 µL nuclease‑free water.
Measure concentration (Biospec‑Nano) and dilute to 0.05 pmol fragment⁻¹.
If concentration insufficient, repeat extractions and ethanol precipitate; keep molar variation within ±0.005 pmol.

steps.title: Assemble genome by seamless cloning
steps.instruction: Combine the ten purified fragments into a full‑length ΦR26 genome using NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly.

substeps.instruction: For each fragment, adjust to 0.05 pmol (≈1 µL per fragment).
In a tube, mix 1 µL of each fragment (total 10 µL), 10 µL 1× NEBuilder HiFi Master Mix, add nuclease‑free water to 20 µL total.
Incubate at 50 °C for 2 h (extended from 1 h to improve yield).
Prepare 0.8 % agarose in 1× TAE, pour 3‑5 mm gel.
Mix 5 µL assembly product with 1 µL 6× loading buffer, load with 1‑kb ladder.
Run electrophoresis at 100 V for 45 min, stain with EtBr 15 min, image to confirm ligation.
Purify assembly product: combine 15 µL of assembly mix (unused for imaging) with 100 µL nuclease‑free water.
Add equal volume PCI (phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol), mix gently, centrifuge 18,000 × g 5 min RT, discard upper aqueous phase.
Add equal volume CIA (chloroform:isoamyl alcohol), mix, centrifuge 18,000 × g 5 min RT, transfer upper aqueous layer to new tube.
Measure OD260/280 and OD260/230 (BioSpec‑Nano) to confirm purity.
Quantify DNA concentration with Quantus Fluorometer using QuantiFluor dsDNA assay.
If protein contamination remains, repeat PCI/CIA extraction before electroporation.

steps.title: Prepare competent Pa12 cells
steps.instruction: Generate electrocompetent P. aeruginosa Pa12 cells for linear DNA electroporation.

substeps.instruction: Inoculate 5 mL LB with 20 µL Pa12 glycerol stock, incubate overnight at 37 °C with shaking.
Dilute 100 µL overnight culture into 9.9 mL fresh LB (1:100).
Grow at 37 °C, shaking 3–4 h until OD600 ≈0.6.
Centrifuge 10,000 × g 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in sterile water.
Transfer 1 mL suspension to a new tube, centrifuge 10,000 × g 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL 10 % glycerol; repeat wash once more.
Pipette the pellet ~100 times with a 1‑mL tip to remove ions; if resistance too high, add small TE buffer.
Centrifuge 10,000 × g 5 min, discard supernatant, add 500 µL 10 % glycerol gently, transfer 100 µL to cuvette, measure resistance (target <10 kΩ).
Aliquot competent cells and store at –80 °C (stable 6–12 months).
